trust_decision.summary: The package's only public function, purify(), parses untrusted HTML with HTMLParser and re-serialises its own node tree; Node.attributeString interpolated every allowed attribute value verbatim between double quotes, so a value containing a '"' closed the attribute and the rest of the value became live attributes (handlers). The published fix neutralises this by entity-encoding " < > and bare & at the single attribute-emission site.

landing_point.why: The advisory is attribute injection, so the first place an engineer looks is where attribute name/value pairs are turned back into markup text: the string concatenation inside Node.attributeString, which writes `name="value"` with no encoding of value.

fix_sites.entry_point: XHTMLPurifier.purify(text, dontFormat, catchErrors) — the package's single exported function (XHTMLPurifier.js:970-987, re-exported at index.js:1, typed at index.d.ts:6)
fix_sites.module_kind: public API module / core sanitizer serializer (single-file library, no routing layer)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The advisory, its test and the fix are all about quoted attribute values; the uncovered route is character-data content, which the report never mentions and the fix never touches, so a solver can argue 'text escaping is a different, out-of-scope concern' (or that HTMLParser's tag-splitting already makes text safe).

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Values that are already entity-encoded (e.g. `<script src="something">`) and legitimate `&` in href query strings or `data-latex` must survive as single entities; an unconditional `&` -> `&` escape double-encodes them and breaks the round-trip the project's own 'works on escaped html' test asserts (the published fix's negative lookahead at fix.diff:18 exists only to keep these untouched).

O6_input_shapes: double quote embedded in a single-quoted source attribute (the report's shape): `<a href='http://x/' class='c" onmouseover="x'>`
single-quoted, double-quoted and unquoted source attribute values (the tokenizer regex has all three branches and the unquoted branch `[^>\s]+` also admits a literal `"`)
a bare `&` that is not a valid character reference (encoded to `&`)
non-string values coerced with String(value) before encoding

O8_uncovered_routes.route:
Character data is emitted completely unescaped by the text-node serializer, so a raw `<` that the tokenizer hands over as text (it splits character data at `<` and keeps the `<` as the last character of the text chunk) is concatenated with the following text node into live markup: purifying `

a ` returns `

a

`.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is text context, not attribute context; the advisory names attribute injection, and the published fix never touched this path, so 'the text path was always like that / is a different concern' is a plausible dismissal.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, ~70 lines above the landing point (XHTMLPurifier.js:81 vs XHTMLPurifier.js:148); the tokenizer that produces the raw text is one file away (HTMLParser.js:105-152)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: an encodeText()/escapeText() sibling of the attribute encoder, applied in TextNode.prototype.toString
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The same developer who added 'encode when serializing' to attributeString would naturally add the text-side encoder in the sibling serializer of the same class, and would likely leave one context (text vs attribute) unencoded exactly as happened here.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second attribute-copy/serialisation path in Node.clone(), used when active formatting elements are reconstructed (XHTMLPurifier.js:259)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Cloning is the obvious place for someone to re-quote attributes by hand for the reconstructed `a`/`strong` elements instead of reusing attributeString.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a per-attribute validator table (scheme regex per name) replacing the inline href-only `^https?:\/\/` check
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The inline href special case invites a refactor into the allowed_attributes table, and a maintainer can easily cover href but miss src/cite/longdesc or miss re-encoding for the newly validated attribute.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: an extra export such as purifyFragment()/sanitizeAttributes() that serialises without going through attributeString
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: A single 3-argument function is a tempting thing to wrap; a convenience export is a normal library growth step and would be the sort of entry point a report would not mention.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a consumer of the unused `escaped` field (backslash-escaped quote variant) that writes values with backslashes instead of entities
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The tokenizer already computes a second, differently-escaped form of every value that nothing uses; a maintainer could route some output through it, producing a JavaScript-style escape that is wrong for HTML.

O9_family: cross-site scripting (CWE-79) via improper output neutralisation/attribute injection (CWE-116) in an HTML sanitizer's serialiser

O10_build.toolchain: Node.js + npm; no build step, no bundler, no transpiler; devDependencies mocha and chai (package.json:34-37), no `scripts` block so tests run via the mocha CLI
O10_build.project_tests: test.js — 10 mocha/chai specs at the pinned commit covering plain paragraphs, formatting tags, escaped-html round-trip and tables (test.js:6-66); no security tests, and the regression test added by the fix (fix.diff:31-44) is not present at the pinned commit

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Encode or strip only the double quote in the attribute value (value.replace(/"/g, """) or drop values containing a quote), which fixes the reported example and leaves `<`/`>`/bare `&` and the unescaped text-node serializer alone

out_of_scope_notes: Adjacent, not pursued: the attribute-name allowlist lookup uses plain-object truthiness (XHTMLPurifier.js:130-137), so names equal to Object.prototype members (`__proto__`, `constructor`, `toString`) pass the allowlist and are emitted; values are still encoded, so this does not give an XSS breakout and is outside this advisory's encoding protection.
unverified: Exploitability of the text-node route was traced by hand through HTMLParser.js:105-152 and XHTMLPurifier.js:78-107; the project's code was not executed (no running allowed), so the payload string was not confirmed against a browser.
Only the provided advisory summary was available (no network, no advisory file), so O13 and the recall assessment are judgement calls.
